Opening of Kendriya Vidyalayas
†*21. PROF. RAM DEO
BHANDARY: W ill the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Kendriya Vidyalayas in
some States are not being opened despite
heavy demands of the public as
Governments of these States are not making
the land and buildings available for the
purpose as a result of which these schools
are being shifted to other States;
(b) if so, the reasons for such negative
reaction and mentality of these State
Governments;
(c) whether Government are solving this
issue through administrative pressure and
dialogue with such States; and
(d) if so, its present status and the
alternative arrangements available with
Government?
Enrolment in Higher Education
*22. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has targeted to increase the enrolment rate
in higher education;
(b) if so, how much intake is likely to
be increased and the current intake in all
the universities;
(c) whether Government have created
adequate infrastructure like laboratories,
libraries, classrooms, teachers, etc. to
achieve the target; and
(d) if so, the details thereof ?
Expenditure on renewable energy
*23. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE
ENERGY be pleased to state:
(a) the total amount spent for the
production and setting-up units for
renewable energy during the last five years,
State-wise; and
(b) the total production of renewable
energy, State-wise?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

8
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
ISO-9000 certificate to schools
*24. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Rajakiya
Pratibha Vikas School in Dwarka, in South-
West Delhi has been awarded ISO-9000
certificate; if so, the details of efforts made
by the school for achieving excellence;
(b) the number of other Government
schools possessing this kind of excellence;
and
(c) the steps Government have taken to
encourage competitiveness for achieving
such kind of excellence?
Proposals from Madhya Pradesh
under APDRP
†*25. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH :
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Madhya
Pradesh Government has sent a proposal
involving Rs. 7.71 crore to the Central
Government for Accelerated Power
Development and Reform Programme in
Jhabua, Wadwani, Pithampur, Bardwah and
Sanawad districts in that State;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether these proposals have been
approved; and
(d) if not, the present status thereof
and by when the same are likely to be
approved?
Effect of corruption in education
*26. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any study report recently from UNESCO's
International Institute for Educational
Planning, which reveals that various shades
of corruption afflict the education system
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto; and
(c) the details of steps taken or proposed
to be taken against such erring institutes in
the country for securing the career of
students?
Achievement of total literacy
*27. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are taking steps
to achieve 100 per cent literacy by 2010 and
were planning to increase it by 25 per cent
this year, to ensure 100 percent literacy by
2010 and allotted Rs. 32,352 crore for
education in 2007-08 budget, 31 per cent
higher than last year's allocation; and
(b) if so, to what extent both Central and
State Governments have taken steps to
implement the schemes to achieve this goal?

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:

†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Danger of global warming
136. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
Minister of  EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai
finds a place in the list of areas that face the
danger of global warming;
(b)  if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether other coastal cities are also
included in the list; if so, the names thereof;
and
(d)  the steps/measures taken/being
taken by Government  in this regard?
Threat of global warming
†137. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether there was any consensus
among international delegations in Bangkok
on 4th May, 2007 that to face the threat of
global warming, the harmful effects of
emission of green house gases should be
curbed;
(b)  whether there was also any
consensus on the report of international
panel on climatic changes in this meeting,
in which it was stressed to take immediate
steps to lessen the increase of 2 degree
celcius temperature all over the world; and
(c)  if so, the steps taken, so far, to face
the threat of global warming in the country?
NCR towns under seismic zone
†138. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA: W ill the Minister of
EARTH SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether Government have any
information about the towns in the NCR
region which come under the seismic zone;
(b)  the details of residential buildings
in these towns which are vulnerable to
earthquake; and
(c)  the action plan of Government to
instruct the residents  to carry out
retrofitting, in order to increase the
earthquake resistant capacity of their
houses?

34
Advanced communication facility for
Tsunami warning system
139. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister of  EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether,  in order to speed up India's
tsunami warning system, it is proposed to
set up an advanced communication facility,
to enable immediate transfer of information
from data collection centres along the
coastline to a central institute;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c)  by when the new system would
start functioning and how far this would
help to cut the delays in timely relaying of
information, to control loss of life and
property?
Setting up of mega food parks
140. SHRIMATI. N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of  FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether the high-level committee
on manufacturing, headed by the Prime
Minister, approved five mega food parks
in the country on a fast track mode;
(b)  whether it is also a fact that one
park is going to be set up in Andhra Pradesh
through public private partnership;
(c)  if so, the details thereof;
(d)  whether any budgetary grant is
provided to the above parks;
(e)  if so, the details thereof;
(f) whether the above food parks are
part of the 30 food parks to be set up in the
Eleventh Five Year Plan; and
(g) if so, by when the above five food
parks are going to be set up?
Storage facility for fruits and
vegetables
141. SHRI TARIQ ANW AR: Will the
Minister of   FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a)  whether it is a fact that a large
quantity of fruits and vegetables are wasted
in the country every year due to shortage
of proper storage facility;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c)  the steps taken by Government in
this regard?
Pending proposals for food processing
industries
142. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of   FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state the details
of the proposals for food processing
industries lying pending with his Ministry
as on date, indicating the period of
pendency of each proposal, the details in
giving clearance to each of these proposals
and by when all these proposals are likely
to be cleared?
Projects for food processing in Punjab
143. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of   FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a)  whether his Ministry has initiated
any new projects for food processing in
Punjab during the last two years and so far
during 2007;
(b)  if so, the details thereof, project-
wise, indicating particularly the location of
each project; the funds required for their
completion, project-wise; and
(c)  by when all these projects are likely
to be completed, project-wise?

35
Potential in food processing sector

Minister of   FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether India produces around 10
per cent of world's fruits and vegetables
and has a good potential in food processing
sector;
